item.title: Arizona mom used her flip-flop to fight off a coyote attacking her 4-year-old daughter
item.description: Brittany Cardinal was fighting off a coyote attack with a flip-flop when the animal bit her face while she shielded her 4-year-old daughter.
item.content:encoded:
An Arizona mom out in her neighborhood flying a kite with her 4-year-old daughter a couple of Sundays ago found herself in a fight with a coyote that refused to back down.

The coyote had started nipping at the little girl, according to mom Brittany Cardinal, and before she knew it, mom was swinging her flip-flop at it.

"We had gone outside because it was windy. And my daughter’s like, 'oh, let's fly a kite,'" Cardinal said, reports AZ Family.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

A normal activity on a windy Sunday afternoon. That was until mom heard her daughter scream and saw the coyote going after the girl.

"I picked her up and then I started yelling at it, thinking, of course, it’s going to go away, and then it didn't," Cardinal said. "So then I took off my flip-flop, and I was trying to scare it with that by like trying to hit it."

As the mom tried to fight off the coyote and get it to leave them alone, she fell. The coyote then bit her on the face.

ALASKA MOOSE HUNTER MIRACULOUSLY SURVIVES AMBUSH BROWN BEAR ATTACK, SAYS HE 'BLACKED OUT'

"I always hear people say like, 'you don’t feel the pain when like trauma like that happens,' and I mean, I really didn’t feel any pain," Cardinal said of the bite. "I just felt like the pressure of it."

Mom and daughter were eventually able to get away from the feisty coyote and make it back home. Mom had lacerations and puncture wounds on her face from the bite.

Arizona Game and Fish officials have removed several coyotes from the area following the incident and are testing them for rabies. They said that Cardinal did everything you're supposed to do during a coyote attack.

I guess everything except for getting bitten on the face. That I highly doubt is in the protocol. But everything else she did correctly.

Alex Flickinger, public affairs community liaison for Arizona Game and Fish, said, "You fight back, you yell at the animal, be loud with it, throw rocks, whatever you have to do to get that animal to just run off."

item.title: Vikings say Kyler Murray feeling 'pretty good,' participating in team meetings despite serious concussion
item.description: Kyler Murray entered concussion protocol after a vicious hit from Green Bay Packers defenders, but the Vikings head coach says he's feeling good.
item.content:encoded:
Kyler Murray’s start to his Minnesota Vikings career went awry on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium, as he was knocked out of the game with a concussion suffered on just the third offensive possession for the team.

The hits he took from two Green Bay Packers players were vicious, and after he officially entered concussion protocol, the question became whether he would be missing game time moving forward.

Head coach Kevin O’Connell, though, gave an update on his starting quarterback Monday following the Vikings’ come-from-behind victory to beat their NFC North rival, where he said Murray came into the building feeling "pretty good."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

O’Connell confirmed that Murray is in concussion protocol, but he said that the quarterback was participating in team meetings.

The Vikings will be taking it "a day at a time," he said, while the medical staff makes sure Murray passes each step of protocol.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In turn, Murray’s status for Week 2’s matchup against the Chicago Bears, who poured 59 points on the Carolina Panthers in their win on Sunday, is up in the air.

However, Vikings fans seeing the initial blow may have thought Murray would not be available next week. Instead, there is hope so long as he clears protocol.

Before suffering his injury, which came after Murray tucked and ran before a late slide led to the two defenders sandwiching him on the turf, he went 3-of-5 for 18 yards. He also threw an interception on the very first snap of his regular-season Vikings career, throwing a jump ball after the Packers brought a blitz immediately at the line of scrimmage.

Once Murray was off the field, veteran Carson Wentz, whom the Vikings kept on after serving in a backup role last season, was called upon to lead Minnesota for the remainder of the home opener.

The result was a composed, effective performance from Wentz, who completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns in the 39-22 win.

Should Murray be unable to play in Week 2, Wentz would almost certainly draw the start for Minnesota, with J.J. McCarthy — the team's first-round pick in 2024 — expected to serve as his backup.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed dismisses questions about Hasan Piker ties on 'Face the Nation,' pivots to groceries
item.description: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed deflected questions about Hasan Piker on "Face the Nation," pivoting to grocery prices.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed rejected questions on Sunday regarding his relationship with Hasan Piker, saying that the race was not about "a Twitch streamer in California."

CBS News' Weijia Jiang asked El-Sayed on "Face the Nation" about Jewish Michiganders' concerns regarding his ties to Piker, the far-left streamer who has appeared with him on the campaign trail.

"There are Jewish voters in your state who are concerned about your relationship with Piker. You have condemned antisemitism but not called out his rhetoric directly. Why not?" Jiang asked.

JEWISH DEM DEFECTIONS THREATEN EL-SAYED IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE DECIDED BY RAZOR-THIN MARGINS

Rather than answering the question, El-Sayed deflected, saying that voters were not asking him about Piker and that they were more focused on the issues impacting their daily lives.

"Weiija, with all due respect, this is the third time you’ve asked about a Twitch streamer in California. I’ve done four events in Michigan this week. You know what didn’t come up? Twitch streamers in California," El-Sayed responded. The candidate said that voters would rather discuss grocery prices, healthcare and the environment, among other things.

"I’m not interested in having a conversation about streamers in California because they are not raising the prices of gas and groceries," El-Sayed added.

El-Sayed is not the first Democrat to push back on questions about Piker. Last month, Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., demanded reporters stop asking her about Piker, saying that "Republicans are trying to make" the race about him.

EL-SAYED TORCHED ONLINE AFTER BRUSHING OFF QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER CAMPAIGN TIES: ‘WHAT A PAL’

"I don’t agree with Hasan Piker on a lot of stuff, and I really don’t agree with him on some of the woman things he said. And I’m still trying to figure out, is it the reason he exercises and looks buff is why he has so many followers," Dingell said during a student town hall with El-Sayed and Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.

Piker has been vocal about his support for El-Sayed, going so far as to call on Democrats to punish those within the party who oppose the Michigan candidate.

"You can't be out here saying like, 'Oh, I'm a centrist Democrat. And I think Abdul is a bridge too far.' That must be punished," Piker said during a stream in August.

While El-Sayed previously appeared with Piker on the campaign trail, he told Semafor in August that he had "no plans" to campaign with the controversial streamer. This came after Piker, who is known for his inflammatory rhetoric and anti-Israel stance, made a remark about Jewish Americans' support for Israel that drew the ire of several Democrats.

"People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during his stream on Aug. 20.

Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., condemned Piker in a statement, calling him "a hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe because he lacks substance."

ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Several other Democratic lawmakers spoke out against Piker after he made the remarks, including Sens. Cory Booker, D-N.J.; Jon Ossoff, D-Ga.; Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.; and Jacky Rosen, D-Nev.; House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Reps. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.; Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.; Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.; Brad Schneider, D-Ill.; and Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.

El-Sayed also responded to Piker's comments, and while he did not condemn the streamer outright, he denounced antisemitism and rhetoric that puts the Jewish community in danger.

"I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote at the time.

"My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk."

item.title: Hochul accused of ‘hit job’ on behalf of teachers’ unions in act of ‘pure censorship’: labor group
item.description: New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul is accused of a free speech "hit job" after signing a law letting Letitia James fine groups contacting union members.
item.content:encoded:
New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul is being accused of conducting a "hit job" on free speech on behalf of teachers unions after she signed a law giving the state attorney general the power to fine groups deemed to be engaged in deceptive communications that falsely appear to be authorized by a union.

Hochul signed a law last week prohibiting people and organizations from using deceptive communications that falsely appear to be authorized by a union or union representative. The law, which took immediate effect, allows Democratic Attorney General Letitia James to investigate and sue to stop alleged violations, including those involving out-of-state groups. Courts can impose fines of up to $1,000 per incident.

In response, the Freedom Foundation, a conservative nonprofit that campaigns against public-sector unions, including teachers’ unions, says New York’s new law is a targeted effort to silence its outreach by making its communications vulnerable to government investigations, lawsuits and fines.

CEO Aaron Withe called the law a "hit job." He said the law "isn’t about protecting anyone," adding that it instead "exists because government unions in New York are terrified of an inconvenient fact: when public employees learn they don’t have to pay union dues, a lot of them stop. So instead of making their case to their own members, union bosses ran to their friends in the legislature and got them to write a law that makes speech illegal."

NATION’S LARGEST TEACHERS UNION UNDER FIRE AS CONTROVERSIAL AGENDA PUTS CENTURY-OLD FEDERAL CHARTER AT RISK

Fox News Digital reached out to Hochul's and James' offices for comment. Fox News Digital also reached out to the New York State United Teachers, United Federation of Teachers and the AFL-CIO for comment.

The law allows James to investigate alleged violations, issue subpoenas and ask a court to block communications deemed deceptive. Courts can impose fines of up to $1,000 per violation, including against organizations outside New York.

The New York State American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (NYS AFL-CIO) praised Hochul’s decision to sign the bill, which she signed along with two other pieces of legislation related to labor rights. Mario Cilento, president of NYS AFL-CIO, remarked that the law will be "holding individuals accountable for fraudulently claiming to be union representatives."

He said the slate of bills signed by Hochul "put workers first."

In an X post, Hochul similarly framed the bills as prioritizing workers, writing, "Today marks a new day with even more protections, because I’ll never stop fighting for our workers."

"New York State gave birth to the labor movement. Over the last five years, I have continued that legacy by fiercely supporting the men and women of labor," wrote Hochul.

TRUMP UNLOADS ON AOC, MAMDANI FOR LAUGHING DURING SACRED 9/11 CEREMONY AT GROUND ZERO

Meanwhile, the Freedom Foundation has mailed and otherwise contacted New York public employees, including teachers, to inform them of their ability to leave their unions and stop paying dues. Nearly 7,500 New York public employees have used Freedom Foundation materials to cancel their union memberships, including more than 1,400 so far this year, according to the group.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Withe pointed to the 2018 Supreme Court decision in Janus v. AFSCME, which held that public-sector employees, including public school teachers, cannot be forced to pay union fees for collective bargaining or other speech because that speech can involve political issues protected by the First Amendment.

He said that while the New York law "lets Letitia James fine the Freedom Foundation for outreach the state decides 'impersonates' a union … all we're doing is telling public employees what already gives them: the right to leave their union and stop paying dues."

"This is an anti-speech law aimed at one kind of speaker," said Withe.

He asserted that the New York law was "copied" from a similar measure in Oregon, which the Freedom Foundation is already challenging in the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. He said his organization will "make the same case here."

Fox News Digital spoke with Ryan Walters, former superintendent of Oklahoma public schools and CEO of Freedom Foundation’s education arm, the Teacher Freedom Alliance. Walters called the New York law an example of "pure censorship and targeting of political opponents by Democrats protecting their union bosses."

INSIDE TEACHERS' UNION MAY DAY 'DRESS REHEARSAL' CRITICS WARN WILL 'GROOM' STUDENTS INTO DEM 'FOOT SOLDIERS'

"This is such a canary in the coal mine moment where if New York is allowed to do this - an openly socialist mayor, a governor operating as a tyrant doing the behests of the teachers’ unions - it's going to go on across the country, and our schools will not be able to improve in that kind of environment," he said, adding, "Where New York goes with this is going to be where the other blue states follow."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

He posited that the New York law "shows you how important that power structure is for the Democrat party."

"They have to control the school system to continue to control the country," he said. "Despite elections, they still control these education systems at large. That's why the teachers’ unions are enemy number one of progress in this country and why New York needs to be taken on directly for what they're doing."

item.title: NHS doctor sues after 'bearded' trans patient allegedly exposes himself on women's psychiatric ward
item.description: An anonymous psychiatrist alleged Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust ignored safeguarding concerns by placing biological males on female psychiatric wards.
item.content:encoded:
A psychiatrist took legal action Thursday against the Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust in England, alleging hospital officials ignored safeguarding concerns about men who identify as women being admitted to female psychiatric wards despite a landmark U.K. Supreme Court ruling on biological sex.

The Christian Legal Centre, which is representing the psychiatrist under the name "Dr. A," said in a press release that "vulnerable female patients, including survivors of sexual violence, have been detained in psychiatric wards under unlawful NHS policies which allow men to access these wards and intimate places, such as showers, because they merely identify as women."

"The public, politicians and the media need to know that mentally ill men and women are being detained together on mixed-sex wards whilst the NHS pretends its wards are single-sex," Dr. A said in the press release.

The dispute follows the U.K. Supreme Court's unanimous April 2025 decision that the terms "woman," "man" and "sex" in the Equality Act 2010 refer to biological sex. The ruling permits biological males who identify as women to be excluded from certain women-only spaces while leaving existing protections against discrimination based on gender reassignment intact.

FEMALE VIRGINIA OFFICER SUES POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHARING LOCKER ROOM WITH BIOLOGICAL MALE

Despite the ruling, Dr. A claims that her repeated requests about how the NHS Trust was complying with the law were "met with delay, resistance and suggestions that the judgment might be challenged in the European Court of Human Rights."

Dr. A also said that the day after the Supreme Court ruling, the Trust reportedly told staff there would be no immediate changes for patients.

Her claim gained attention after she alleged that a biological male patient who identified as a woman was placed on a women's psychiatric ward where he exposed male genitalia to female patients. According to a report from U.K. outlet The Times, the patient was temporarily moved to a male ward following complaints before being returned to the women's ward.

Dr. A said the incident was described to her by another consultant working at the hospital.

"He said that there had been a man with a beard and full male genitalia who had been exposing himself to female patients and they were unhappy," she explained.

FEMALE INMATE SUES WASHINGTON STATE AFTER ALLEGED ATTACK BY MALE-BORN PRISONER IN WOMEN'S FACILITY

Dr. A said she pursued legal action after concluding that her efforts to raise the issue internally over the past three years had not resulted in adequate changes. She filed an Employment Tribunal claim against the NHS Trust alleging unlawful workplace discrimination and harassment over her protected gender-critical beliefs, claiming the Trust ignored her safeguarding warnings and failed to bring its policies into line with the Supreme Court’s ruling on biological sex.

"As a senior doctor, I could not remain silent while women’s privacy and dignity were being compromised. I raised these concerns because I believe every patient has a right to be treated with compassion and to have her sex recognized when intimate care, accommodation and personal safety are involved," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

The NHS Trust now acknowledges the Supreme Court ruling on its website and said it is reviewing its existing rules.

"As a result, we are actively undertaking an audit of our policies, procedures and processes in order to reflect this clarification in the law," the Trust said.

MED SCHOOL DEANS COME UP EMPTY IN TENSE HEARING WHEN ASKED POINT BLANK IF MEN CAN HAVE BABIES: 'RIDICULOUS'

The Trust's review came as national NHS guidance also remains unresolved. NHS England's current guidance, first issued in 2019, says transgender patients should be accommodated according to their gender presentation, including for toilets and bathing facilities, but NHS England added after the Supreme Court ruling that the guidance is "currently being reviewed."

The existing guidance also states providers should generally have a "zero-tolerance approach" toward mixed-sex accommodation and should protect patients' safety, privacy and dignity.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission pointed Fox News Digital to its new statutory Code of Practice, which took effect in August and outlines how service providers should apply the law to single-sex services.

"In separate or single-sex services, a trans man will be excluded from the men-only service because his sex is female, and a trans woman will be excluded from the women-only service because her sex is male," a spokesperson said.

The EHRC press office also directed Fox News Digital to provisions requiring service providers to consider whether women's safety, privacy or dignity would be jeopardized by sharing a service with men. The guidance specifically tells providers to consider whether women are likely to be undressed, have limited ability to leave or choose an alternative service, or are receiving services connected to male violence against women.

Sonja Shaw, a candidate for California superintendent of public instruction and girls' sports advocate, sharply criticized policies she says put women's safety at risk.

"Sex is real, and girls and women deserve privacy, safety, and fairness, not institutions that pretend otherwise," she told Fox News Digital. "Hospitals putting bearded men who identify as women into female psychiatric wards reads as the next step of a process that has been perpetuated by this perverse political agenda."

"It is the same failure we already see in schools that put biological males into girls’ sports, locker rooms, and bathrooms," Shaw continued. "And it won’t stop until we address the root problem and codify protection for biological women’s right to private and protected spaces. Stop sacrificing women and girls at the altar of ideology. Female psychiatric wards turned into male cosplay zones isn’t healthcare. It’s malpractice against vulnerable women."

item.title: Deadly bacteria detected as NYC orders emergency cleaning of cooling towers
item.description: A health expert discusses why Legionnaires' disease outbreaks keep striking the South Bronx and other historically marginalized NYC areas.
item.content:encoded:
Health officials ordered the immediate remediation of 10 rooftop cooling towers in the South Bronx after preliminary testing detected Legionella bacteria amid a growing Legionnaires’ disease cluster that has sickened nine people and left one dead.

The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene issued orders to clean and disinfect the sites. Among the affected structures are cooling towers at major hubs, including Yankee Stadium and Lincoln Hospital.

As public health workers work to clean the equipment, experts note that recurring outbreaks in these neighborhoods highlight deeper systemic vulnerabilities.

NYC LEGIONNAIRES' DISEASE OUTBREAK KILLS FOURTH VICTIM, 76 CASES REPORTED

"When we look at outbreaks of Legionnaires' disease, in New York City, we almost always see it in the Bronx or Harlem," Dr. Tyler Evans, CEO of the Wellness Equity Alliance and former first chief medical officer for New York City, told Fox News Digital.

"A lot of times, we see risk of infections taking place in historically marginalized communities."

The department identified the cluster following a surge in cases dating back to late August. Tests confirmed traces of Legionella in 10 of 24 sampled towers, according to city health officials.

PCR (polymerase chain reaction) tests return results quickly, but cannot distinguish between live and dead bacteria. Culture tests to confirm live bacteria can take up to two weeks, prompting city health officials to order immediate cleaning out of caution.

Late-summer weather has compounded the issue. High temperatures create ideal breeding grounds for bacteria inside industrial air-conditioning systems, which add water to the surrounding air, Evans noted.

HEART ATTACKS AND STROKES RISING WITH EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS, RESEARCH SUGGESTS

"Record-breaking temperatures lead to accelerating the risk of the bacteria basically cooking, getting out to become vaporized, and then producing exposure to other people," he said.

Legionnaires' disease, a severe form of pneumonia, cannot be spread between people, nor is it contracted by drinking tap water, the expert noted. Most healthy individuals are not sickened by exposure, but high-risk populations can face severe health consequences.

"In terms of people ... to be concerned about, it's really older adults — typically 65 and older — or people living with comorbid conditions," Evans said, pointing to underlying factors like diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or compromised immune systems.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Health officials urge anyone who has lived in, worked in or visited ZIP codes 10451 and 10456 since late August to monitor their health.

Key symptoms to watch for include high fevers, severe shortness of breath, chest pain and coughing up bloody mucus.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Evans noted that early medical care is crucial, as the illness responds well to standard antibiotic treatments when caught early.

"Infections fall into different buckets — bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites," he said. "Bacteria are alive. Antibiotics are effective against bacteria because you can kill them, which makes it very treatable."

While city officials have taken quick action to inspect and clean the structures, Evans emphasized that long-term prevention requires sustained public investment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Could we test all cooling towers across New York City on a regular basis during times of risk when it's hotter? Yes," Evans said.

"City health officials do an amazing job, but it costs money. When federal funds are removed from public health, it's very hard to do more when you have less."

Fox News Digital reached out to Yankee Stadium and Lincoln Hospital requesting comment.

item.title: Goo Goo Dolls' John Rzeznik draws line on politics at concerts: 'I'm not going to lecture you'
item.description: John Rzeznik told Rick Beato he won't lecture Goo Goo Dolls fans about politics, saying concertgoers deserve to leave feeling better than they arrived.
item.content:encoded:
Goo Goo Dolls frontman John Rzeznik said Wednesday during an "Everything Music" interview with producer Rick Beato that he refuses to lecture concertgoers about politics because fans from across the ideological spectrum come together for the same reason: to see a show.

While discussing why he believes live music remains important during divided times, Rzeznik said political and religious differences are not what matters when he takes the stage.

"I got people, fans, friends from every walk of life, every political stripe, everything," he said. "And I always stress, we got one thing in common because we're living in weird times. We got one thing in common, and that's we're all here to see a show, and I'm not going to lecture people about anything."

DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’

Entertainment commentator Christian Toto told Fox News Digital that artists can pay a price with their audiences when performances turn into political forums, particularly when celebrity political commentary is already widespread.

"Artists do risk alienating fans when they get on a soap box. That's always been true, but it's even more so today. Why? We're inundated with political screeds, particularly from the rich and famous. In many cases, the arguments being shared are one-dimensional and poorly thought out," Toto said.

"Plus, they're rarely spoken to change hearts or minds," he continued. "The commentary is typically angry and filled with partisan talking points. What does ‘Free Palestine’ mean to someone who questions that community's embrace of violence?"

JOHN RICH CLAIMS JELLY ROLL KNEW HE’D LOSE HALF HIS FANS OVER POLITICAL COMMENTS

Toto pointed to the cost of attending major concerts as another reason artists could frustrate audiences by devoting stage time to politics.

"Concert tickets are insanely high in 2026," he said. "Imagine forking over so much money and then, mid-concert, you get a political lecture. Who wants that? Kudos to Rzeznik for understanding that simple truth, one that eludes many ego-driven rockers."

Rzeznik’s approach mirrors comments Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger made earlier this year. Fox News Digital reported in July that Jagger viewed his job during concerts as helping audiences forget their problems for a few hours rather than preaching to them.

GOO GOO DOLLS SINGER HOSPITALIZED WITH PNEUMONIA; BAND CANCELS CONCERTS IN SOUTH AFRICA

Explaining his approach to performing, Jagger made clear he did not believe audiences came to see him for political instruction.

"I don't want to lecture them," Jagger said.

Other rock stars have faced a different reception after bringing politics into performances. In June, Bruce Springsteen and The Black Crowes frontman Chris Robinson faced backlash from some concertgoers following political remarks onstage.

Rzeznik told Beato he wants Goo Goo Dolls fans to instead leave a concert feeling better than when they arrived.

"I'm going to play a bunch of songs that, you know, and we're all going to leave here, and we're going to be happier and better for it. That's it," Rzeznik said.

The comments came amid renewed attention for Goo Goo Dolls and their 1998 hit "Iris." The band released a reimagined version of the song with Steve Aoki in March and spent summer touring with Neon Trees. An anniversary edition of the band's 1998 album "Dizzy Up the Girl," which featured "Iris," is scheduled for release Oct. 2.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rzeznik for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Carnegie Mellon 'deeply concerned' by professor's 'hostile and threatening posts' about Charlie Kirk's death
item.description: Carnegie Mellon University says it is reviewing Uju Anya's social media posts invoking "Kirkmas" near the anniversary of Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
Carnegie Mellon University says it is reviewing "hostile and threatening social media posts" by professor Uju Anya after she invoked "Kirkmas" and "Kirk Mubarak" around the first anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s assassination.

Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was assassinated Sept. 10, 2025, while speaking at Utah Valley University during his American Comeback Tour.

The Pennsylvania university also told Fox News Digital Friday that Anya is currently on voluntary professional leave and is not teaching courses on campus during the current academic year.

UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE CONDEMNS FLYERS APPEARING TO CELEBRATE CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION

item.title: Yet another Dem ripped online for 'inventing racism' as lawmakers peddle debunked ‘lynching’ claims
item.description: Rep. Shontel Brown faces backlash after claiming lynchings are rising in the United States, despite cases being widely debunked as suicides.
item.content:encoded:
An Ohio congresswoman is facing major blowback online after suggesting that lynchings are on the rise in the United States, despite that claim being widely debunked last week.

"In the last year, there’s been an alarming increase in Black Americans found dead hanging from trees. We know what that has meant throughout our history," said Rep. Shontel Brown, D-Ohio, on X. "That’s why I’ve joined [Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass.] to demand a federal investigation into possible lynchings."

Fox News Digital reviewed some high-profile cases after Pressley's letter to the DOJ demanding "thorough, transparent, and comprehensive federal investigation into every hanging death of a Black individual across the United States." Last week, Pressley and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., posted about the letter on their X accounts, drawing blowback and widespread debunking of the suggestion that there has been an uptick in lynchings.

GOVERNOR BLAMES ACTIVISTS IN NOLAN WELLS CASE FOR ‘STOKING DIVISION,’ OFFICIAL SAYS FBI PROBING THREATS

Ocasio-Cortez called the incidents "racial terror" and likened them to "widespread modern-day lynchings."

An investigation into the March death of a 21-year-old man found hanging from a tree in Cobb County, Georgia, concluded that the man was alone at the time, and no foul play is suspected.

Police in Charlotte, North Carolina determined that a 16-year-old found hanging from a tree in May died by suicide. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Department in Florida came to the same conclusion in the similar death of a 27-year-old in June. At least three more similar cases were ruled suicides.

If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

One is still under investigation. The high-profile case of Tasia Fortune, also found hanging from a tree, is being treated as a homicide. A Black male suspect, Jarques Ratliff, has been arrested.

The facts didn't stop Brown from perpetuating the claim of prolific hangings.

SOCIALIST POLITICIANS ARE 'MORE RACIST THAN THE KKK,' SAYS BLACK DEM OFFICIAL URGING VOTERS TO DITCH EL-SAYED

"For generations, trees were used as instruments of terror against Black Americans," Brown said in a video attached to the post. "Lynching was used to intimidate entire communities, and those deaths almost always went without justice and without accountability. So, when Black Americans are found hanging from trees today, in unfamiliar places and under circumstances that raise serious questions, we cannot look the other way."

For the post, Brown was widely condemned online.

"Inventing racism. Purposely misleading and pernicious," said actor Dean Cain of "Superman" fame.

KARMELO ANTHONY VERDICT DRAWS ANTI-WHITE RAGE AND LIES FROM RADICAL DEM CONGRESSWOMAN, ANGRY ACTIVISTS

"No no and no," said a popular X user with more than 250,000 followers. "I get it, Democrats have spent decades creating racism where none exists, especially right before an election. But nobody is buying this, especially when we know the majority were suicides and oh yeah, the man arrested for the homicide is a black guy. Stop."

"This is how Democrats stir up racial divide when there isn’t one," said podcaster Don Keith, adding that Brown was trying to "blame black suicides and homicides on white people now."

"Apparently it’s 2019 again and Jussie Smollett is walking to a Subway…," said podcaster Margo Chatting, referencing the actor's infamous hate crime hoax wherein he claimed he was attacked by White Trump supporters, only for an investigation to find that he faked the attack.

Author Dan Friedman laid into the congresswoman.

"You know these were all suicides, except one domestic violence murder in which the perpetrator was a black man. Some of these people were literally seen hanging themselves on security cameras," he said.

"You cannot possibly be stupid enough to believe that mobs of white racists are abducting black men at random for no reason, hanging them from trees, disappearing without a trace and that law enforcement officials who are often black are covering it up. So, if you are not stupid, you are lying and being disingenuous. The question is, why?"

Brown's office did not return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Construction rig collapses on 3 cars in Miami, traps workers as fire erupts
item.description: A dramatic scene unfolded in Miami's popular Brickell neighborhood after heavy equipment crashed onto vehicles and a construction container, sending four people to the hospital.
item.content:encoded:
Four people were taken to the hospital Monday after a construction rig toppled onto three vehicles and a construction container in Miami, trapping two workers and igniting a vehicle fire, authorities said.

Miami Fire Rescue responded to the scene in the city's popular Brickell neighborhood near Southeast 12th Street and Brickell Bay Drive after the drilling rig collapsed at around 8 a.m.

"Miami Fire Rescue responded after a drilling rig fell onto three vehicles near SE 12 Street and Brickell Bay Drive," Miami Fire Rescue said in a post on X. 

"The Technical Rescue Team units worked to safely free two trapped victims in a crushed container. Fortunately, the 4 patients transported were in stable condition."

MIAMI WAITRESS ACCUSED OF EXTORTION & THREATENING TO SEND INTIMATE PICS AFTER LEARNING SHE WAS THE OTHER WOMAN

Firefighters rescued two construction workers, ages 27 and 29, who were trapped inside the crushed construction container, Miami Fire Chief Robert Hevia said during a news conference.

Crews simultaneously extinguished a fire that erupted after the rig crushed a BMW, Hevia said.

"To be able to see the crane falling, pull the car in reverse and pop out of the back while the car’s on fire, really incredible," he said, describing how the BMW's driver managed to escape the burning vehicle.

The rig also crushed two unoccupied parked vehicles, he said.

CRANE ARM COLLAPSES INTO MIAMI CONDO ROOFTOP POOL AREA AS WORKERS CLING TO DANGLING STRUCTURE

The two workers, the 47-year-old rig operator and the BMW driver were all taken to local hospitals with minor injuries, he said. Hevia also said all 18 construction workers at the site were accounted for.

"It was a very complex scene with a fire that was occurring, our crews were putting out the fire and our technical rescue team working simultaneously to cut through the Conex box, the construction box, and they were able to successfully extricate the two victims," Hevia said.

Earlier Monday, the Miami Police Department urged motorists to avoid the area.

"Due to a crane collapse, Brickell Bay Drive is currently closed between SE 12th Street and SE 13th Street. Motorists are encouraged to avoid the area, seek alternate routes, and expect delays. Please use caution and follow the direction of officers on scene," Miami Police wrote on X.

ONLYFANS MODEL COURTNEY CLENNEY SENTENCED TO SIX YEARS IN BOYFRIEND’S KILLING

Officials have not said what caused the collapse. Hevia said the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is investigating the incident.

According to NBC 6 South Florida, the collapse occurred at the site of billionaire Ken Griffin's planned Citadel headquarters.

Miami Fire Rescue and Citadel could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

item.title: Suddenly, Steve Sarkisian is singing a completely different tune about playing Ohio State
item.description: Steve Sarkisian's bold fourth-down calls fueled Texas' 24-23 comeback over Ohio State, shaking up the College Football Playoff picture in week two.
item.content:encoded:
We're only through week two of the 2026 college football season, and already, the College Football Playoff picture has received a significant shake-up.

One of the preseason favorites, the Oregon Ducks, suffered a shocking loss on the road to Oklahoma State, in a game where they gave up 554 yards defensively and an incredible 237 yards on the ground. To a team that had lost 12 games in a row heading into Saturday.

Oklahoma suffered a substantial blow to its hopes of getting an at-large playoff spot after losing on the road to a 1-0* Michigan team that spent the week getting buried by national media. And of course, the game of the week, maybe the game of the season, turned in the most shocking result of the weekend. Not so much for the outcome, but how it happened.

NEW AP POLL TOP 25 PUNISHES OHIO STATE, OKLAHOMA, OREGON, TEXAS JUMPS TO NO 1 AFTER BIG COMEBACK

The Texas Longhorns completed a miraculous comeback over the Ohio State Buckeyes in Austin, with a season-defining 24-23 win. With an extremely tough schedule on tap, it gave the Longhorns some breathing room for a potential playoff berth, and one of the best resume boosters any team can or will have for 2026.

Head coach Steve Sarkisian has received some well-deserved praise for how he handled the second half. Instead of playing not to be blown out, Sark coached like he was trying to win a game, even in his own territory. Twice, he went it for on fourth and long, including a fourth and nine from the Texas 42-yard-line late in the third quarter. Twice, the Longhorns were successful.

ARCH MANNING AND TEXAS LONGHORNS ERASE 20-POINT DEFICIT TO STUN OHIO STATE IN SHOCKING COMEBACK FOR THE AGES

Coaching with urgency allowed Texas to get back in the game, and eventually win it. After the win, Sarkisian took a bit of a victory lap, blasting other programs for scheduling cupcake opponents while the Longhorns hosted Ohio State.

"We could be like other teams and play Jones Junior High and win 66-0," he told reporters. "I don’t know what that does for us. Tonight we found out that we can (win big games)."

That's great, the Longhorns-Buckeyes game was college football at its best. Two historic blue blood programs, squaring off on campus and not at Mercedes-Benz Stadium or some other unaffiliated NFL venue. It gave Arch Manning a signature moment in Austin, demonstrated that Texas, despite their obvious flaws and mistakes during the game, is still dangerous and capable of winning a championship.

It's also a complete 180 from how Sarkisian was talking about the game after last season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

For a quick refresher, the Longhorns missed out on a spot in the College Football Playoff in the 2025-2026 regular season because they finished 9-3 and there were more deserving teams ahead of them. Texas lost on the road to Ohio State early in the season, sure, but also lost to a dismal 4-8 Florida team, were blown out by the Georgia Bulldogs, and struggled to close overtime wins against bad Kentucky and Mississippi State teams.

After beating Texas A&M to finish the regular season, Sark went ballistic on the selection committee.

"It would be a disservice to our sport if this team is not a playoff team when we went and scheduled that non-conference game (Ohio State)," he said in an interview. "Because if we’re a 10-2 team, it’s not a question. But, we were willing to go play that game. So, is that what college football is about? Don’t play anybody and just have a good record, or play the best and put the best teams in the playoff. And, we’re one of the best teams."

There's a problem with that, obviously, which is that the Longhorns weren't left out because they lost to Ohio State by seven points. They were left out because they lost to 4-8 Florida and struggled with Kentucky and Mississippi State. Objective, analytics and efficiency driven ranking systems like ESPN's SP+ put the Longhorns at No. 22 in the final rankings before the playoff selection. That's why they were left out of the playoff, they didn't deserve to be included.

As a result of this abhorrent "disservice," Sark went off about scheduling teams like Ohio State. In December 2025, he said he would "re-evaluate" future schedules because he didn't believe tougher strength of schedule was properly rewarded.

Now? He's pounding his chest over playing Ohio State instead of an FCS team, because the Longhorns won. Had they lost, and finished the season 9-3 and missed out again, he'd be complaining.

To be fair to him and the Longhorns, it's a tricky balancing act, weighing schedules. Because, on the one hand, both teams can and should be credited for playing this game. On the other hand, Sark is essentially arguing that the outcome shouldn't matter. Winning or losing is irrelevant, because credit for scheduling it should come first. That's effectively what he said on Monday, per The Athletic.

"Quite frankly, Ohio State should be rewarded for playing in this game against us, and so that’s my goal," Sarkisian said. "Time will tell, you know. And this isn’t crying over spilled milk. I don’t think we got rewarded for going to Columbus last year in Week 1."

We all want more games like this, but if there are no stakes, no reward based on performance and outcome, what's the point? What might make sense is some concrete criteria, a combination of forward-looking efficiency ratings, and strength of resume rankings, along with human evaluation of that combination, to pick the playoff teams. At least then subjectivity would be diminished, there would be more rewards for playing tough schedules, and Sark would have less to complain about after his undeserving team isn't selected.

But that makes too much sense for college football, so don't expect any changes anytime soon.

item.title: Macklemore doubles down after getting kicked off Ed Sheeran tour after pro-Palestine stance
item.description: Macklemore claims Robert Kraft rallied stadium owners to give Ed Sheeran an ultimatum over his "Free Palestine" remarks on the U.S. Loop Tour.
item.content:encoded:
A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Ed Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour."

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."

Macklemore was slated to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour.

PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS

On Monday, Macklemore addressed the announcement and doubled down on his stance.

"I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," he wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families."

BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM

"The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence. More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don’t lose sight of that."

WATCH: MACKLEMORE OPENED HIS PERFORMANCE WITH AN ANTI-ICE AND ISRAEL RANT

On Sept. 4, Macklemore opened for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. He repeatedly chanted "Free Palestine" while a slideshow played on the screen behind him, showing footage from the war in Gaza.

Several fans were upset by the performance, including an Instagram page called "Stop Antisemitism." The page shared a video criticizing Macklemore, calling the move "awful." Pink reposted the video to her own Instagram story, which started a new wave of backlash from people criticizing her for seemingly being pro-Israel.

In his Instagram post, Macklemore said he and Sheeran, who he considers a "friend" and "brother," had "some difficult conversations" in the days following his remarks.

"The type of talks rooted in love and respect for one another that still end in a place of fundamental disagreement," he wrote. "Nothing I’m writing here is out of spite or because I want to tear down his character. But as I told Ed multiple times on the phone, our friendship can’t change my responsibility to tell the truth about what happened."

The rapper claimed Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, told Sheeran that Macklemore "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium.

Kraft issued a statement defending his decision to influence the rapper's removal from the tour. 

"Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," the statement read.

"Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line."

The statement continued: "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive.

"Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium.

"I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."

In Macklemore's post, he said, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Ed was in a f---ed up position," he wrote. "He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, 'I don’t take sides.'"

WATCH: PINK SLAMS MACKLEMORE OVER PRO-PALESTINIAN COMMENTS

CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT

Macklemore said he's been saying "Free Palestine" onstage for almost three years and questioned why he was being removed from the tour now.

"What I said at MetLife I have been saying on stages around the world for almost three years. So why is it an issue now? Because now I’m sharing a stage with one of the biggest artists in the world, in some of the biggest stadiums in America. At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk. If I kept doing the shows, saying ‘Free Palestine,’ with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next? The stage becomes resistance. Maybe that’s why this time it became so important to silence me."

"And one of the most effective ways to enforce that silence has been to weaponize the accusation of antisemitism. Antisemitism is real," he continued. "And that is exactly why the word matters too much to be used as a shield against criticism of the Israeli state. When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying ‘Free Palestine’ gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn’t protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability."

While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he said he stands by his position.

"I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine. But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on."

Representatives for Sheeran did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Deshaun Watson remains the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback but that comes with an expiration date
item.description: Todd Monken says Deshaun Watson will start against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but mounting pressure and a Week 3 home opener could force a change.
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns are sticking with Deshaun Watson despite the understandable conversation among their fan base and in the media that the quarterback should be benched following a season-opening loss.

"I anticipate that Deshaun will be our starter," coach Todd Monken announced on Monday.

Monken gave his reasons for keeping Watson in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. But, make no mistake, the patience for continuing this course comes with an expiration date.

And that date is the Week 3 game against the Carolina Panthers.

First the news of the day: Monken, having watched the tape of a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, believes he saw enough from Watson after 693 days of not playing to keep him in the starting role.

"It's only been two weeks he's gotten all the reps," Monken said, referring to the fact the Browns had a starting QB competition in training camp and the practice repetitions were split between Watson and Shedeur Sanders.

"And there were some really good things on film," the coach added, "some things that you can build on. And there were some others that operationally we got to get better at.

"There's concepts that, you know, there's only so many looks you get from week to week, be it red zone concepts, third down concepts. And I did think that when he had time, when he understood the concepts, he didn't play tentative, that he let it rip.

"So there was a lot of things to build on. Wasn't perfect, of course not. Otherwise, we wouldn't have scored as few points as we did. But I'd like to see how we can build on that."

DESHAUN WATSON THROWS INTERCEPTION FIVE SNAPS INTO 2026 SEASON AS BROWNS GET OFF TO ROUGH START

That's as close to a full-throated endorsement any quarterback who completed 16 of 22 passes for a modest 205 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception could hope to get.

But let's be clear, Watson's time as the starter is not indefinite. In fact, it is likely to last only one more week unless he shows improvement against the Buccaneers.

Why?

Circumstances are working against him. And ownership is going to take those circumstances under advisement, multiple NFL sources believe.

So what circumstances?

The Browns play a Tampa team led by quarterback Baker Mayfield, who was the No. 1 draft pick in 2018 by the Browns.

But the Browns jettisoned Mayfield in a July 2022 trade, ending a contentious breakup after four years. Once Cleveland acquired Watson from Houston in March of 2022, Mayfield’s future was effectively over.

The Browns chose Watson over Mayfield, but Mayfield has gone on to significant success with the Bucs. And Watson has been a major disappointment with the Browns.

So it would be an embarrassment for the Browns and a grim reminder of that misguided 2022 decision if Mayfield outplays Watson. It would serve as a strong suggestion the club finally needs to move in a different direction.

But there could be a more compelling reason to bench Watson after another unremarkable week and that is all about the venue where the games are scheduled.

The Browns opened this season on the road and will be on the road in Tampa. They will have their regular-season home opener in Week 3 against the Panthers.

And that's when the fractured relationship Watson has with Browns fans could be on full display. It was on display in the preseason when Browns fans booed Watson with gusto.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

After that game, Watson was somewhat critical of the fans for booing him. He believed it was disrespectful and said if he was named the starter he'd feel like he was playing 17 road games.

That Aug. 22 game was the last time Watson played at home. Can anyone imagine how Browns fans would react to Watson if he returns a month later, having criticized them and also having lost or played poorly the first two games of the regular season?

It would be ugly.

So Watson probably gets just one more week to rally and give fans and his team a reason to believe he's turned a corner of sorts.

"We got to play better around him. We got to call it better," Monken said. "And he's going to play better."

item.title: Russia readies new 500-mile missile as weapon expert warns of 'terminal end game surprises'
item.description: Russia plans to test a new 800-km ballistic missile by year's end, with an analyst warning its advanced maneuverability could strain Ukraine air defense.
item.content:encoded:
Moscow is preparing for a final test of a new ballistic missile capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away and potentially maneuvering in ways that could challenge Ukraine’s already strained air defenses, a defense analyst warned Monday.

The warning comes as Ukrainian military officials said that Russia could conduct the test in the coming months and potentially in live-fire strikes.

"According to our estimates, Russia plans to conduct final tests of a new type of ballistic missile with a range of up to 800 km by the end of this year," Vadym Skibitskyi, deputy head of the Defence Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU), said at a meeting of the Ukraine-NATO Interparliamentary Council, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

"If, for instance, this 800-kilometer missile has more advanced maneuverability, well then that's going to create greater problems for Ukraine in that they're going to need the more sophisticated interceptors to get them," Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told Fox News Digital.

RUSSIA DEPLOYS NORTH KOREAN MISSILE UNIT TO UKRAINE; MOSCOW-PYONGYANG AXIS DEEPENS: REPORT

"This means terminal maneuvers that weave a little bit so that the defender doesn't quite know where it's going or what trajectory it will have," Karako said.

"Another possibility is that they just figured out a way to make some kind of 800-kilometer missile more cheaply or in large numbers," the expert said of the Russians.

Karako said developments in precision-guided munitions, along with a broader shift away from unguided weaponry, could offer clues about the type of missile Russia will launch.

NEXT-GENERATION MISSILE DEFENSE AT MISSION SPEED

"Everyone is going for increased maneuverability," Karako explained. "Just about every gravity bomb that we have has some kind of terminal guidance for precision," he said, specifically of the U.S. arsenal.

"In a similar way, a moment's not too far in the future where you don't really have that many purely ballistic missiles."

"You have things that may be ballistic for a good part of their path, but are also equipped with maneuvering reentry vehicles or some kind of terminal end game surprises," he warned.

Meanwhile, according to Ukraine's DIU, Russian forces may try to strike targets in western Ukraine during the missile tests as a live-fire demonstration, which Karako said is standard practice in wartime.

"This is a business-as-usual arrangement where you might do lots of developmental testing and then formally field and then have your operational testing," the expert said.

RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

"There are all kinds of norms being broken, though, because it is, after all, wartime, and so it may well be the case that some of this stuff is tested — maybe not the first time — but some of the early tests are done, frankly, in the field in Ukraine," he added.

The missile would, however, fall into a category once prohibited under the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, Karako warned.

Signed by President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in 1987, the INF Treaty required the United States and the Soviet Union to eliminate ground-launched ballistic and cruise missiles with ranges between 500 and 5,500 kilometers (roughly 310 to 3,400 miles).

The United States withdrew from the treaty in 2019 amid alleged Russian violations.

"This range is one that was formerly prohibited by the INF Treaty that capped ballistic and cruise missiles at 500 kilometers in range," Karako said.

"To some extent, you see Russia filling that gap, which is understandable and reasonable. Of course, they were violating the INF Treaty, which was why the United States got out of it."

PENTAGON PLOTS NEW NUCLEAR OPTIONS FOR TRUMP AS AMERICA’S BIGGEST ADVERSARIES RAISE STAKES: REPORT

Missiles and artillery have been central to Russia's campaign against Ukraine since the start of the war in 2022. Ukrainska Pravda reported Aug. 10, citing Ukrainian military intelligence, that production of Russia's primary missile types had reached between 110% and 120% of monthly targets.

According to the Kyiv Independent, Russia fired at least 1,858 missiles of various types at Ukraine from the start of 2026 through Aug. 27.

"This is what's hitting Ukraine on a daily and weekly basis. And so it's in that broader context of that demand for standoffs of various kinds that you see new things pop up," Karako said.

RUSSIA THREATENS STRIKES ON UK MILITARY TARGETS, ‘CATASTROPHIC CONSEQUENCES’ OVER UKRAINE

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy highlighted the growing strain on air defenses in an interview with Deutsche Welle at a Canadian military base in North Bay Sept. 12.

"I want to have 100-120 [interceptor missiles] for these difficult months, especially the cold months," Zelenskyy said. "We'll see how many months this winter lasts — that is, these cold months: one, two, three. We don't know. This is truly a major challenge."

"It is the case that Russia really is on a wartime footing, and they really have mobilized their defense industrial base to be cranking these (missiles) out like sausages," Karako said.

"There was a point in which everything was going to the front, everything was going to Ukraine."

"There have been other reports more recently that suggest that Russia may be keeping some in reserve," Karako added.

"There are lots of worries. If you're in Poland, if you're in Romania, if you're in the Baltics, you're worried about the Russians."

item.title: Kawhi Leonard finally returns to Raptors after NBA disciplined Clippers for salary cap rule circumvention
item.description: Kawhi Leonard heads back to the Toronto Raptors after the NBA stripped the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks for salary cap violations.
item.content:encoded:
Kawhi Leonard is officially heading back to the Toronto Raptors, and it comes after the NBA disciplined the Los Angeles Clippers for breaking the league’s salary cap rules.

Leonard was at the forefront of a previously agreed-upon trade between the two franchises, but there was a question about whether it would go through.

Now, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported Leonard, who helped the Raptors win the 2019 NBA title, will be heading back north of the border in exchange for 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round picks as well as a 2027 first-round pick swap between both teams.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Clippers will also receive forward Brandon Ingram, shooting guard Gradey Dick, and second-round picks for the 2030 and 2033 NBA Drafts.

And yes, the Clippers will be getting the two first-round picks from the Raptors despite the league stripping them of five first-round picks, which were their own in 2031 and 2033 as well as others in 2029, 2030 and 2032.

NBA LEVIES ASTONISHING PENALTY AGAINST CLIPPERS OVER CAP CIRCUMVENTION INVOLVING STEVE BALLMER, KAWHI LEONARD

After an investigation, the NBA found the Clippers to be in violation of its salary cap rules for allegations that Leonard specifically received impermissible benefits from the franchise, including being paid $28 million for a "no-show job." This was done as a way to get around the salary cap.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is also suspended from all league and team activities for one year for "knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities, for approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement agreement with Mr. Leonard, and for his failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA’s circumvention rules," a league statement said.

Leonard, through his agent Harrison Gaines, issued a statement after the league’s discipline came down on the Clippers.

" Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am," he said, per ESPN. "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap. For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with.

"As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The deal between the teams was originally agreed in June, but it wasn’t expected to become official until July 6. However, the league’s investigation into the Clippers put the deal on hold after it was alleged that the Clippers evaded the salary cap while signing Leonard to a $103 million free agent deal in July 2019. Both teams agreed it would wait to make the deal official until after the NBA’s investigation concluded.

As part of the discipline, Ballmer was also fined $30 million, while president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank received a six-month suspension without pay. Gillian Zucker, the team’s president of business operations, was also suspended without pay for one year.

Leonard may be going to Toronto, but he faces discipline as well. He was fined $700,000 by the NBA, while his business advisor, Dennis Robertson, was banned from engaging in future business dealing with the league.

Ballmer noted that he would be accepting the league’s discipline and wouldn’t be seeking any legal filings to challenge its ruling.

Leonard made his seventh All-Star appearance last season, where he averaged 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game across 65 contests for Los Angeles.

item.title: Carrie Underwood fires up another SNF heater, Collinsworth was DISGUSTED & naked Sydney Sweeney angers the mob
item.description: Carrie Underwood kicked off her 14th season on Sunday Night Football as Cris Collinsworth couldn't hide his disgust with the Dallas Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

What a weekend.

Goodness gracious, did I miss that. College football all day Saturday. Texas-Ohio State madness to end the night. And then we finally got to watch the RedZone countdown clock hit all zeroes yesterday for the first time since January.

Makes me tear up every year!

Sure, my Dolphins were horrible, but I knew that coming in. I was just glad to watch a QB not crumble the second a defender got within 10 yards of him. What a pleasure.

NFL WEEK 1 TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS FLASH CONTENDER UPSIDE, BEARS EXPLODE AND PACKERS COLLAPSE

Serious question: Was that one of the best 1 p.m. Week 1 slates we've ever had? Admittedly, I don't remember all of them, but I also don't recall that many touchdowns being scored during the 1 p.m. hour in a long time.

Did any of my anytime touchdown parlays hit? Nope. Not one. But still, what a rush!

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Carrie Underwood fires up the Sunday Night Football fastball for yet another season.

How great was it to end our weekends with Carrie again last night? Just felt right.

What else? I've got Cris Collinsworth being just DISGUSTED by the Dallas Cowboys, and the internet is pissed about two things from over the weekend: Sydney Sweeney getting naked, and Holly Rowe.

Two VERY separate things, I might add. Phew.

Grab you a Boston Cream donut for National Cream-Filled Donut Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

Let's go ahead and get this outta the way real quick before we launch into another week ...

Boston cream donuts are the only good creme-filled donuts. Those other ones with the whiter filling inside? They're horrible. They're knockoffs.

Yes, I realize that sounded sexual. There's nothing I can do about it. I'm describing a donut. It's not easy.

And yes, I also realize doughnut is the traditional spelling. I don't care. It's donut. This is America.

Whatever that means.

OK, now that our weekly Ted Talk is outta the way, let's get this class started the same way we ended our first NFL Sunday ...

With the return of Carrie Underwood:

I'm happy to report that most of the feedback online was positive. Earlier this summer, we had a couple internet trolls try to get Carrie fired before her 14th season on SNF, claiming she was past her prime.

Hogwash!

Sure, you still had some naysayers. You always will in today's society. I assume some of them don't like Carrie because she was at Trump's inauguration two years ago? I don't know. That's the only thing I can think of.

Some are calling for her to "retire." Others didn't love that NBC seemingly remixed the classic intro just a touch, although I didn't really notice much of anything.

Regardless, any day that ends with Carrie leading us into Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth is a good day. It's perfect. It's America at our best.

Welcome back, football. And welcome back, Collinsworth!

"Here's a guy who STINKS at covering tight ends!"

Amazing. Cris was just disgusted by the Dallas Cowboys last night. He couldn't believe the garbage he was watching. I imagine Dallas fans felt the same way.

Side note: Speaking of things I'd love to retire, can we please try something else on Sunday Night Football for a while? We get Cowboys-Giants EVERY SINGLE YEAR. Most of the time, it's the season-opener. It never fails.

I understand the TV markets. I do. I know why NBC does it, but goodness, it ain't like Sunday Night Football needs any propping up in the ratings department. It's routinely the most-watched show every single year. By a wiiiiiiiiiiiiiide margin.

That being said, if this game weren't in New York, we might not have got this little gem out of Collinsworth in the second quarter:

"I felt like there was so much raw emotion in this building. 9/11. And I mean, it was just raw."

Incredible. Nobody does it quite like Cris. Elite stuff. Like Carrie, he's untouchable.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night ... of MORE football! Don't forget, we get our first Monday Night Football game of the year in a few hours.

Chiefs-Broncos. Mahomes off the ACL. Nix off the broken ankle. Jaylen Waddle. Travis Kelce. Joe and Troy. What a blessing.

God, I love this country.

You know what I specifically love? Bitter women who are currently blaming Sydney Sweeney on the downfall of women's sports:

Oh give me a break. This is just insane.

"I can’t describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this," said Ariarne Titmus, a former Australian swimming champion. "Not only is it a kick in the face to every woman who has dedicated her life to perfecting her craft, but every woman who enjoys sports for what it really is — teamwork, friendship, dedication, excellence, unity. How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman’s body and sexualizing women’s sport is still a thing?"

Please. What are we doing here? Sydney Sweeney doing a mostly-naked commercial for sports gambling has literally zero impact on women's sports. It hasn't set women's sports back decades. It hasn't sexualized anything.

It's called GOOD MARKETING.

Do these ladies know who does 99% of the sports betting in this country? Men. This ad is geared towards GUYS.

Guys like sports. Guys like gambling on sports. And, yes, guys like half-naked women. I'm not breaking news to anyone here. It's just the truth.

Sydney Sweeney and Novig didn't reinvent the wheel with this ad. They used their brains and put together quite literally the easiest marketing campaign of all time. Let's not make it more than it is.

Speaking of fake outrage ... anyone see this Holly Rowe-Steve Sarkisian after Texas's stunning win Saturday night?

The Big Js are FURIOUS at Sark today:

I don't know Holly Rowe at all. I've never met her. I only know her from a few weeks ago when she cried into the camera because there was a big crowd at a women's basketball game in Canada. Seriously. She did that.

But I'm not going to pass judgement on someone I don't know.

Here's what I do know: These postgame interviews are so dumb. Frankly, so are the halftime interviews. Do we really need them? Talk to Arch. Talk to the players. We don't need to hear from the coaches. It's all the same. It's all coach speak. It's all fluff, including the questions.

Here's how this would've gone, by the way:

"Sark, how big is this moment for the program?"

"It was pretty big, Holly. We just beat the No. 1 team in the country. That's always big."

"What were your emotions like"

"I was pretty happy. We won. Just really proud of the guys."

There. I just did the whole interview for you! You're welcome.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Let's enjoy some more FOOTBALL tonight.

Here's more Sydney on the way out.
